svg.aria-label: Nearest neighbours. Neighbours, the k nearest examples: a scatter of grey points on input 1 against input 2, with a new point in the middle; the five points closest to it are blue, joined to it by thin lines and ringed by a circle. The prediction is their average, or the share of each category. Number of neighbours, k sets the smoothness: points scatter around a hump against one input; with k = 1 the prediction is a jagged line that jumps to every point, with k = 7 it is a smooth hump; with k = all it is a dashed flat line at the average. Few neighbours follow the noise; all of them give one average everywhere. Beyond the data, flat at the edges: the same kind of smooth line rises and falls through the data, then stays level in shaded regions with no data at either end, because past the last example the neighbours never change. A note says distance treats every input alike, so the inputs are put on one scale first.
svg.text: Distance treats every input alike, so the inputs are put on one scale first.
